content:
Money problems in Class 4 combine decimals with real shopping — bills, change, unit costs. Practical, high-frequency Olympiad content. This guide covers what the Maths Olympiad Class 4 money chapter tests, the facts to know, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Money chapter tests

  • Rupee-paise arithmetic with decimals
  • Bills and totals (quantity × rate)
  • Making change
  • Unit cost and multiple purchases

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 rupee = 100 paise; ₹8.75 = 875 paise.
  • Line up decimal points when adding or subtracting money.
  • Cost of many = unit cost × number; unit cost = total ÷ number.
  • Change = money given − total cost (check by adding back).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Dropping the paise digits in a subtraction.
  • Multiplying when the problem asks for unit cost (divide).
  • Forgetting to total all items before finding change.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Money Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Meera buys 4 kg of apples at Rs 25 each and 3 kg of guavas at Rs 18 each at the fruit stall and hands over a Rs 200 note. What change should she receive?
questions.explanation: Bill = Rs 25 x 4 + Rs 18 x 3 = Rs 100 + Rs 54 = Rs 154. Change = Rs 200 - Rs 154 = Rs 46.

questions.q: A dealer buys a bicycle for Rs 1500 and has to sell it for Rs 1275. What is his profit or loss?
questions.explanation: Cost price Rs 1500 is more than selling price Rs 1275, so it is a loss of Rs 1500 - Rs 1275 = Rs 225.

questions.q: A toy shop owner buys a remote-control car for Rs 1200 and sells it for Rs 1450. Find the profit or loss.
questions.explanation: Selling price Rs 1450 is more than cost price Rs 1200, so it is a profit of Rs 1450 - Rs 1200 = Rs 250.

questions.q: Aditya receives Rs 60 every week and saves it for 5 weeks. He then buys a wrist band set costing Rs 235. What amount remains?
questions.explanation: Savings = Rs 60 x 5 = Rs 300. Left = Rs 300 - Rs 235 = Rs 65.

questions.q: Meera buys 6 notebooks priced at Rs 24 each. How much does she pay in all?
questions.explanation: Cost of 6 items = Rs 24 x 6 = Rs 144.

questions.q: Vikram buys 5 identical toy whistles for Rs 175. What is the price of each whistle?
A trader buys a study table for Rs 925. He sells it and earns Rs 145 as profit. What was the selling price?
questions.explanation: Selling price = cost price + profit = Rs 925 + Rs 145 = Rs 1070.

questions.q: Kabir buys 3 pens at Rs 12 each and 2 notebooks at Rs 15 each, and pays with a Rs 100 note. How much change does he get?
questions.explanation: Bill = Rs 12 x 3 + Rs 15 x 2 = Rs 36 + Rs 30 = Rs 66. Change = Rs 100 - Rs 66 = Rs 34.

questions.q: A shopkeeper buys a wall clock for Rs 350 and wants a profit of Rs 60. At what price should he sell it?
questions.explanation: Selling price = cost price + profit = Rs 350 + Rs 60 = Rs 410.

questions.q: The canteen serves Rohan's table 4 plates of idli at Rs 17.50 each and 2 glasses of juice at Rs 10 each. What is the bill for the table?
questions.explanation: 4 plates of idli cost Rs 17.50 x 4 = Rs 70; 2 glasses of juice cost Rs 10 x 2 = Rs 20. Total = Rs 70 + Rs 20 = Rs 90.

faq.q: How do you find the change?
faq.a: Subtract the total cost from the money handed over. For ₹100 given on a ₹68.25 bill, change = ₹31.75.

faq.q: How do you find unit cost?
faq.a: Divide the total by the number of items: ₹96 for 8 books = ₹12 each.
